messages:
eva: Canary deploy in eu-west failed during pre-hook, SOPS/vault-agent can't fetch key for vault://proj/key. Blocking GPU canary nodes. Anyone seen this before?
sam: Which error are you seeing? paste logs?
olivia: Logs from vault-agent on the canary pod: ```time="2026-03-18T10:15:02Z" level=error msg=\"failed to fetch secret\" error=\"egress quota exceeded: bytes_sent=125MB limit=100MB\"```
chris: Wait, egress quota? That sounds like the new NAT gateway SNAT fix from last week — we added a prefix list for eu-west to block some ranges. Could be hitting our vendor egress metering.
sre-ryan: Confirming: cloud console shows NAT gateway throttling for the eu-west subnet at ~10:12 UTC. Lots of small TLS connections from vault-agent. Looks like the agent is doing per-secret fetches and we crossed billed egress bucket.
ev a: Canary is configured to fetch SOPS keys per-pod at init, so that would multiply. How long until quota resets?
sre-ryan: Quota resets in ~40m unless we request emergency lift. We have a short window before scheduled canary retry.
sam: Workarounds: 1) switch the canary to use sealed-secrets or pre-inject the decrypted envs, 2) point vault-agent to regional internal proxy that has separate egress, 3) temporarily skip sops pre-hook for canary. Which is fastest?
jen: Fastest is a Helm override to disable the sops pre-hook in the canary release. I can push a patched values.yaml to the canary branch and trigger a GitOps sync.
olivia: I don't love disabling secret verification but it's fine for a 1-replica canary if we limit scope. Also we should avoid storing plaintext in the repo — use sealed-secrets with ephemeral keys.
chris: If we do sealed-secrets, that still needs controller to fetch key on cluster startup. But we can put a pre-sealed secret in the canary namespace that doesn't require network egress.
sam: Short-term plan: jen sends helm override, olivia pre-seals the smallest env var set and commits to canary branch. I'll open a Terraform ticket to request temporary NAT egress bump for eu-west and track cost.
devops-bot: Pipeline status: canary-helm-override -> pending job queued by jen (CI #4523).
jen: Pushed https://git.company/repo/infra/commit/abc123 with values.canary.sops.enabled=false and added sealed-secret for CANARY_MIN_ENV. Triggering Flux reconcile.
devops-bot: Flux sync started for infra/canary at commit abc123.
eva: Re-deploying canary now. Fingers crossed.
devops-bot: Canary rollout event: pod/canary-0 -> Created.
chris: Can someone confirm that vault-agent logs are no longer attempting egress?
sre-ryan: Verified on pod logs: ```time="2026-03-18T10:29:10Z" level=info msg=\"no remote fetch configured, using sealed secret mount\"```
olivia: Canary passed healthchecks, GPU node registered and jobs started. :white_check_mark:
sam: I'll follow up with a small RFC for batching vault-agent requests and a fallback to regional proxy to avoid hitting egress quotas again. Also adding a telemetry counter for per-pod egress bytes.
eva: Thanks everyone. Filing incident follow-up and cost note. We'll keep the temporary Helm override until we have a better persistent mitigation.
jen: I'll revert the override once the NAT quota change is in place or we've rolled the batching change.
sre-ryan: Filing ticket: CLOUD-3211 "eu-west NAT egress cap caused vault-agent failures for canary; add regional proxy and batching". Assigned to sam.
eva: Closing thread — canary unblocked and running.
